line: Young or old, we expect little change ahead. Researchers call this an illusion.
Every body has hard days. The wise expect them, and stay calm.
credit: Tiruvalluvar · Tirukkural 627, tr. G. U. Pope

line: A climber called Grandma Whitney took up jogging. Why? It made climbing much easier.
So pack before you go. Out for a day? Take bread for a week.
First in the bag, a strong body. The mind cannot carry the load alone.
credit: Montaigne · Of the Education of Children

line: Next, a breath habit: slow, deep and steady, until the mind finds balance.
And a mind like a mirror: it meets everything and holds on to nothing.
credit: Zhuangzi · ch. 7, tr. H. A. Giles, 1889

line: But stored bread is not eaten bread. Only what you practise becomes you.
So practise every day. Busy? Do one asana. But never skip completely.
Your daily bread: Ashtanga. Asana for strength, breath for lightness, turning inward for calm.
credit: Gheranda Samhita 1.10-11 · tr. S. C. Vasu
